## One-Sentence Summary

A compact, portable home-security device that installs without tools or Wi-Fi, offering app control, on-device alerts, and shared access for renters, students, and travelers.

## Problem

The creators argue that traditional residential security is expensive, invasive, and built for homeowners, leaving students, renters, and travelers without a practical way to feel secure in dorms, sublets, and temporary stays. They cite barriers such as landlord approval, drilling, and long-term contracts as key blockers.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product is a lease-friendly smart security device designed to be set up in minutes without tools or approvals. It works without Wi-Fi (with an optional cellular version) and provides peace of mind across dorms, apartments, and travel accommodations through mobile alerts, local alarms, and simple controls.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   **Burglar detection:** When a door opens, the system checks for nearby approved devices (e.g., a user's phone); unrecognized entries are flagged as unauthorized.

-   **Versatile keypad:** Users can arm/disarm without a phone.

-   **Lock reminder:** Sends a notification if the user leaves a defined safe zone without locking the door.

-   **Alarm system:** Triggers an on-device alarm upon intrusion and sends instant mobile alerts to approved users.

-   **Real-time tracking:** Shows last-seen time/place, enables a "ping" to locate the device, and includes a Lost Mode.

-   **Multi-user/device access:** Multiple approved users can control the device and receive notifications.

-   **Cellular connectivity (optional):** Maintains alerts during internet outages; paired with the built-in battery for continued operation.

-   **Mobile app control:** Monitor status, receive alerts, and adjust settings remotely.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Stated audiences include college students, renters, and travelers using dorms, apartments, sublets, and short-term stays. The device is positioned for everyday protection in shared or temporary spaces and for situations with unreliable networks.

## Development Status

According to the page, development began in late 2022. The team references "final prototypes," a brief demo, and a product evolution overview.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

The team states it is moving from final prototypes into scaled production and has prepared contingency plans for potential schedule shifts, supported by relationships with suppliers and manufacturing partners. No specific calendar dates are listed.

## Risks & Challenges

Acknowledged risks include supply-chain delays during scale-up and the complexity of supporting multi-user, multi-device scenarios across varied environments. Mitigations include established partner relationships and a focus on keeping the experience simple but secure.

## Team & Partnerships

The founders describe themselves as students and renters who built the product around their lived constraints. They reference suppliers and manufacturing partners without naming them. The team also discloses the use of an AI text-to-speech system for a campaign video voice-over.

## What's Included

A mobile app experience for remote control/alerts is described. The campaign also mentions an initial free trial period for the product's subscription service. Variants include a Wi-Fi model and an option with cellular connectivity.

## Technical Details

Explicit details include optional cellular connectivity, an on-device keypad, an on-device alarm, approved-device proximity checks, and a built-in battery supporting operation during internet outages. Specific dimensions, materials, and OS requirements are not listed.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team emphasizes ongoing commitment to a simple, secure experience as the product scales; ongoing software update cadence or warranty terms are not detailed.

## One-Sentence Summary
A compact, portable home-security device that installs without tools or Wi-Fi, offering app control, on-device alerts, and shared access for renters, students, and travelers.

## Problem
The creators argue that traditional residential security is expensive, invasive, and built for homeowners, leaving students, renters, and travelers without a practical way to feel secure in dorms, sublets, and temporary stays. They cite barriers such as landlord approval, drilling, and long-term contracts as key blockers.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is a lease-friendly smart security device designed to be set up in minutes without tools or approvals. It works without Wi-Fi (with an optional cellular version) and provides peace of mind across dorms, apartments, and travel accommodations through mobile alerts, local alarms, and simple controls.

## Key Features & Capabilities
-   **Burglar detection:** When a door opens, the system checks for nearby approved devices (e.g., a user's phone); unrecognized entries are flagged as unauthorized.
-   **Versatile keypad:** Users can arm/disarm without a phone.
-   **Lock reminder:** Sends a notification if the user leaves a defined safe zone without locking the door.
-   **Alarm system:** Triggers an on-device alarm upon intrusion and sends instant mobile alerts to approved users.
-   **Real-time tracking:** Shows last-seen time/place, enables a "ping" to locate the device, and includes a Lost Mode.
-   **Multi-user/device access:** Multiple approved users can control the device and receive notifications.
-   **Cellular connectivity (optional):** Maintains alerts during internet outages; paired with the built-in battery for continued operation.
-   **Mobile app control:** Monitor status, receive alerts, and adjust settings remotely.

## Target Users & Use Cases
Stated audiences include college students, renters, and travelers using dorms, apartments, sublets, and short-term stays. The device is positioned for everyday protection in shared or temporary spaces and for situations with unreliable networks.

According to the page, development began in late 2022. The team references "final prototypes," a brief demo, and a product evolution overview.

The team states it is moving from final prototypes into scaled production and has prepared contingency plans for potential schedule shifts, supported by relationships with suppliers and manufacturing partners. ## Risks & Challenges
Acknowledged risks include supply-chain delays during scale-up and the complexity of supporting multi-user, multi-device scenarios across varied environments. Mitigations include established partner relationships and a focus on keeping the experience simple but secure. The proposed pilot test plan is designed to specifically address the challenge of validating multi-user scenarios.

The team emphasizes ongoing commitment to a simple, secure experience as the product scales; ongoing software update cadence or warranty terms are not detailed. The proposed pilot test with a student group would be part of the planned post-launch validation efforts.

## One-Sentence Summary
A compact, portable home-security device that installs without tools or Wi-Fi, offering app control, on-device alerts, and shared access for renters, students, and travelers.

## Problem
The creators argue that traditional residential security is expensive, invasive, and built for homeowners, leaving students, renters, and travelers without a practical way to feel secure in dorms, sublets, and temporary stays. They cite barriers such as landlord approval, drilling, and long-term contracts as key blockers.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is a lease-friendly smart security device designed to be set up in minutes without tools or approvals. It works without Wi-Fi (with an optional cellular version) and provides peace of mind across dorms, apartments, and travel accommodations through mobile alerts, local alarms, and simple controls.

## Key Features & Capabilities
-   **Burglar detection:** When a door opens, the system checks for nearby approved devices (e.g., a user's phone); unrecognized entries are flagged as unauthorized.
-   **Versatile keypad:** Users can arm/disarm without a phone.
-   **Lock reminder:** Sends a notification if the user leaves a defined safe zone without locking the door.
-   **Alarm system:** Triggers an on-device alarm upon intrusion and sends instant mobile alerts to approved users.
-   **Real-time tracking:** Shows last-seen time/place, enables a "ping" to locate the device, and includes a Lost Mode.
-   **Multi-user/device access:** Multiple approved users can control the device and receive notifications.
-   **Cellular connectivity (optional):** Maintains alerts during internet outages; paired with the built-in battery for continued operation.
-   **Mobile app control:** Monitor status, receive alerts, and adjust settings remotely.

## Target Users & Use Cases
Stated audiences include college students, renters, and travelers using dorms, apartments, sublets, and short-term stays. The device is positioned for everyday protection in shared or temporary spaces and for situations with unreliable networks.

## Development Status
According to the page, development began in late 2022. The team references "final prototypes," a brief demo, and a product evolution overview.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

## One-Sentence Summary
A compact, portable home-security device that installs without tools or Wi-Fi, offering app control, on-device alerts, and shared access for renters, students, and travelers.

## Problem
The creators argue that traditional residential security is expensive, invasive, and built for homeowners, leaving students, renters, and travelers without a practical way to feel secure in dorms, sublets, and temporary stays. They cite barriers such as landlord approval, drilling, and long-term contracts as key blockers.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is a lease-friendly smart security device designed to be set up in minutes without tools or approvals. It works without Wi-Fi (with an optional cellular version) and provides peace of mind across dorms, apartments, and travel accommodations through mobile alerts, local alarms, and simple controls.

## Key Features & Capabilities
-   **Burglar detection:** When a door opens, the system checks for nearby approved devices (e.g., a user's phone); unrecognized entries are flagged as unauthorized.
-   **Versatile keypad:** Users can arm/disarm without a phone.
-   **Lock reminder:** Sends a notification if the user leaves a defined safe zone without locking the door.
-   **Alarm system:** Triggers an on-device alarm upon intrusion and sends instant mobile alerts to approved users.
-   **Real-time tracking:** Shows last-seen time/place, enables a "ping" to locate the device, and includes a Lost Mode.
-   **Multi-user/device access:** Multiple approved users can control the device and receive notifications.
-   **Cellular connectivity (optional):** Maintains alerts during internet outages; paired with the built-in battery for continued operation.
-   **Mobile app control:** Monitor status, receive alerts, and adjust settings remotely.

## Target Users & Use Cases
Stated audiences include college students, renters, and travelers using dorms, apartments, sublets, and short-term stays. The device is positioned for everyday protection in shared or temporary spaces and for situations with unreliable networks.

## Development Status
According to the page, development began in late 2022. The team references "final prototypes," a brief demo, and a product evolution overview.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
The team states it is moving from final prototypes into scaled production and has prepared contingency plans for potential schedule shifts, supported by relationships with suppliers and manufacturing partners. No specific calendar dates are listed. As a proposed next step to validate a core use case, the team plans to conduct a post-campaign pilot test. This planned pilot test would involve a defined user group, such as 50 students in a dormitory setting, to gather evidence on the performance and usability of the multi-user access and notification features in a real-world shared environment. The specific, measurable outcomes we intend to capture include user activation rate, overall system reliability in a multi-user scenario, and notification accuracy, with a proposed target of >95% accuracy in distinguishing authorized from unauthorized entries. Furthermore, as a proposed preliminary step before this pilot, the team plans to conduct a small, focused test of the lock reminder feature's geofencing accuracy in a defined urban environment.

## Risks & Challenges
Acknowledged risks include supply-chain delays during scale-up and the complexity of supporting multi-user, multi-device scenarios across varied environments. Mitigations include established partner relationships and a focus on keeping the experience simple but secure. The proposed pilot test plan is designed to specifically address the challenge of validating multi-user scenarios by measuring the outcomes noted above, including the proposed notification accuracy target. The proposed small test of the geofencing accuracy is intended to specifically address potential performance variability of the lock reminder feature in dense urban settings.

## Team & Partnerships
The founders describe themselves as students and renters who built the product around their lived constraints. They reference suppliers and manufacturing partners without naming them. The team also discloses the use of an AI text-to-speech system for a campaign video voice-over.

## What's Included
A mobile app experience for remote control/alerts is described. The campaign also mentions an initial free trial period for the product's subscription service. Variants include a Wi-Fi model and an option with cellular connectivity.

## Technical Details
Explicit details include optional cellular connectivity, an on-device keypad, an on-device alarm, approved-device proximity checks, and a built-in battery supporting operation during internet outages. Specific dimensions, materials, and OS requirements are not listed.

The team emphasizes ongoing commitment to a simple, secure experience as the product scales; ongoing software update cadence or warranty terms are not detailed. ## One-Sentence Summary
A compact, portable home-security device that installs without tools or Wi-Fi, offering app control, on-device alerts, and shared access for renters, students, and travelers.

## Problem
The creators argue that traditional residential security is expensive, invasive, and built for homeowners, leaving students, renters, and travelers without a practical way to feel secure in dorms, sublets, and temporary stays. They cite barriers such as landlord approval, drilling, and long-term contracts as key blockers.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is a lease-friendly smart security device designed to be set up in minutes without tools or approvals. It works without Wi-Fi (with an optional cellular version) and provides peace of mind across dorms, apartments, and travel accommodations through mobile alerts, local alarms, and simple controls.

## Key Features & Capabilities
-   **Burglar detection:** When a door opens, the system checks for nearby approved devices (e.g., a user's phone); unrecognized entries are flagged as unauthorized.
-   **Versatile keypad:** Users can arm/disarm without a phone.
-   **Lock reminder:** Sends a notification if the user leaves a defined safe zone without locking the door.
-   **Alarm system:** Triggers an on-device alarm upon intrusion and sends instant mobile alerts to approved users.
-   **Real-time tracking:** Shows last-seen time/place, enables a "ping" to locate the device, and includes a Lost Mode.
-   **Multi-user/device access:** Multiple approved users can control the device and receive notifications.
-   **Cellular connectivity (optional):** Maintains alerts during internet outages; paired with the built-in battery for continued operation.
-   **Mobile app control:** Monitor status, receive alerts, and adjust settings remotely.

## Target Users & Use Cases
Stated audiences include college students, renters, and travelers using dorms, apartments, sublets, and short-term stays. The device is positioned for everyday protection in shared or temporary spaces and for situations with unreliable networks.

## Development Status
According to the page, development began in late 2022. The team references "final prototypes," a brief demo, and a product evolution overview.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
The team states it is moving from final prototypes into scaled production and has prepared contingency plans for potential schedule shifts, supported by relationships with suppliers and manufacturing partners. ## One-Sentence Summary
A compact, portable home-security device that installs without tools or Wi-Fi, offering app control, on-device alerts, and shared access for renters, students, and travelers.

## Problem
The creators argue that traditional residential security is expensive, invasive, and built for homeowners, leaving students, renters, and travelers without a practical way to feel secure in dorms, sublets, and temporary stays. They cite barriers such as landlord approval, drilling, and long-term contracts as key blockers.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is a lease-friendly smart security device designed to be set up in minutes without tools or approvals. It works without Wi-Fi (with an optional cellular version) and provides peace of mind across dorms, apartments, and travel accommodations through mobile alerts, local alarms, and simple controls.

## Key Features & Capabilities
-   **Burglar detection:** When a door opens, the system checks for nearby approved devices (e.g., a user's phone); unrecognized entries are flagged as unauthorized.
-   **Versatile keypad:** Users can arm/disarm without a phone.
-   **Lock reminder:** Sends a notification if the user leaves a defined safe zone without locking the door.
-   **Alarm system:** Triggers an on-device alarm upon intrusion and sends instant mobile alerts to approved users.
-   **Real-time tracking:** Shows last-seen time/place, enables a "ping" to locate the device, and includes a Lost Mode.
-   **Multi-user/device access:** Multiple approved users can control the device and receive notifications.
-   **Cellular connectivity (optional):** Maintains alerts during internet outages; paired with the built-in battery for continued operation.
-   **Mobile app control:** Monitor status, receive alerts, and adjust settings remotely.

## Target Users & Use Cases
Stated audiences include college students, renters, and travelers using dorms, apartments, sublets, and short-term stays. The device is positioned for everyday protection in shared or temporary spaces and for situations with unreliable networks.

## Development Status
According to the page, development began in late 2022. The team references "final prototypes," a brief demo, and a product evolution overview.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
The team states it is moving from final prototypes into scaled production and has prepared contingency plans for potential schedule shifts, supported by relationships with suppliers and manufacturing partners. No specific calendar dates are listed. As a proposed next step to validate a core use case, the team plans to conduct a post-campaign pilot test. This planned pilot test would involve a defined user group, such as 50 students in a dormitory setting, to gather evidence on the performance and usability of the multi-user access and notification features in a real-world shared environment. The specific, measurable outcomes we intend to capture include user activation rate, overall system reliability in a multi-user scenario, and notification accuracy, with a proposed target of >95% accuracy in distinguishing authorized from unauthorized entries. Furthermore, as a proposed preliminary step before this pilot, the team plans to conduct a small, focused test of the lock reminder feature's geofencing accuracy in a defined urban environment, with a proposed goal of 90% accuracy within a 100-meter radius. Additionally, the team proposes a small test to validate the built-in battery's performance during a simulated internet outage, specifying a proposed 48-hour continuous operation test.

## Risks & Challenges
Acknowledged risks include supply-chain delays during scale-up and the complexity of supporting multi-user, multi-device scenarios across varied environments. The founders describe themselves as students and renters who built the product around their lived constraints. They reference suppliers and manufacturing partners without naming them. The team also discloses the use of an AI text-to-speech system for a campaign video voice-over.

The team emphasizes ongoing commitment to a simple, secure experience as the product scales; ongoing software update cadence or warranty terms are not detailed. ## One-Sentence Summary
A compact, portable home-security device that installs without tools or Wi-Fi, offering app control, on-device alerts, and shared access for renters, students, and travelers.

## Problem
The creators argue that traditional residential security is expensive, invasive, and built for homeowners, leaving students, renters, and travelers without a practical way to feel secure in dorms, sublets, and temporary stays. They cite barriers such as landlord approval, drilling, and long-term contracts as key blockers.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is a lease-friendly smart security device designed to be set up in minutes without tools or approvals. It works without Wi-Fi (with an optional cellular version) and provides peace of mind across dorms, apartments, and travel accommodations through mobile alerts, local alarms, and simple controls.

## Key Features & Capabilities
-   **Burglar detection:** When a door opens, the system checks for nearby approved devices (e.g., a user's phone); unrecognized entries are flagged as unauthorized.
-   **Versatile keypad:** Users can arm/disarm without a phone.
-   **Lock reminder:** Sends a notification if the user leaves a defined safe zone without locking the door.
-   **Alarm system:** Triggers an on-device alarm upon intrusion and sends instant mobile alerts to approved users.
-   **Real-time tracking:** Shows last-seen time/place, enables a "ping" to locate the device, and includes a Lost Mode.
-   **Multi-user/device access:** Multiple approved users can control the device and receive notifications.
-   **Cellular connectivity (optional):** Maintains alerts during internet outages; paired with the built-in battery for continued operation.
-   **Mobile app control:** Monitor status, receive alerts, and adjust settings remotely.

## Target Users & Use Cases
Stated audiences include college students, renters, and travelers using dorms, apartments, sublets, and short-term stays. The device is positioned for everyday protection in shared or temporary spaces and for situations with unreliable networks.

## Development Status
According to the page, development began in late 2022. The team references "final prototypes," a brief demo, and a product evolution overview.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
The team states it is moving from final prototypes into scaled production and has prepared contingency plans for potential schedule shifts, supported by relationships with suppliers and manufacturing partners. No specific calendar dates are listed. As a proposed next step to validate a core use case, the team plans to conduct a post-campaign pilot test. This planned pilot test would involve a defined user group, such as 50 students in a dormitory setting, to gather evidence on the performance and usability of the multi-user access and notification features in a real-world shared environment. The specific, measurable outcomes we intend to capture include user activation rate, overall system reliability in a multi-user scenario, and notification accuracy, with a proposed target of >95% accuracy in distinguishing authorized from unauthorized entries. Furthermore, as a proposed preliminary step before this pilot, the team plans to conduct a small, focused test of the lock reminder feature's geofencing accuracy in a defined urban environment, with a proposed goal of 90% accuracy within a 100-meter radius. Additionally, the team proposes a small test to validate the built-in battery's performance during a simulated internet outage, specifying a proposed 48-hour continuous operation test. To specifically address the reliability of the core 'approved-device proximity check' feature, the team also proposes a small, focused test to validate its performance in a dense, multi-device environment (like a dorm hallway), with a proposed accuracy target of correctly identifying an authorized user's device 95% of the time within a 3-meter range.

## Risks & Challenges
Acknowledged risks include supply-chain delays during scale-up and the complexity of supporting multi-user, multi-device scenarios across varied environments. Mitigations include established partner relationships and a focus on keeping the experience simple but secure. The proposed pilot test plan is designed to specifically address the challenge of validating multi-user scenarios by measuring the outcomes noted above, including the proposed notification accuracy target. The proposed small test of the geofencing accuracy, with its proposed goal of 90% accuracy within a 100-meter radius, is intended to specifically address potential performance variability of the lock reminder feature in dense urban settings. The proposed small test of the built-in battery's performance is intended to specifically address the reliability of the device during extended power or internet outages. The proposed small test of the 'approved-device proximity check' in a dense environment is intended to specifically address potential signal interference and accuracy challenges in real-world, high-traffic settings.

## Team & Partnerships
The founders describe themselves as students and renters who built the product around their lived constraints. They reference suppliers and manufacturing partners without naming them. The team also discloses the use of an AI text-to-speech system for a campaign video voice-over.

## What's Included
A mobile app experience for remote control/alerts is described. The campaign also mentions an initial free trial period for the product's subscription service. Variants include a Wi-Fi model and an option with cellular connectivity.

## Technical Details
Explicit details include optional cellular connectivity, an on-device keypad, an on-device alarm, approved-device proximity checks, and a built-in battery supporting operation during internet outages. Specific dimensions, materials, and OS requirements are not listed.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team emphasizes ongoing commitment to a simple, secure experience as the product scales; ongoing software update cadence or warranty terms are not detailed. The proposed pilot test with a student group, including the measurement of activation rate and the proposed target for notification accuracy, would be part of the planned post-launch validation efforts. The proposed small test of geofencing accuracy in an urban environment, with its proposed goal of 90% accuracy within a 100-meter radius, is also a planned component of these validation efforts. The proposed small test of the built-in battery's performance is a planned component of these validation efforts. The proposed small test of the 'approved-device proximity check' in a dense environment, with its proposed accuracy target, is a planned component of these validation efforts.

A compact, portable home-security device that installs without tools or Wi-Fi, offering app control, on-device alerts, and shared access for renters, students, and travelers.

## Problem
The creators argue that traditional residential security is expensive, invasive, and built for homeowners, leaving students, renters, and travelers without a practical way to feel secure in dorms, sublets, and temporary stays. They cite barriers such as landlord approval, drilling, and long-term contracts as key blockers.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is a lease-friendly smart security device designed to be set up in minutes without tools or approvals. It works without Wi-Fi (with an optional cellular version) and provides peace of mind across dorms, apartments, and travel accommodations through mobile alerts, local alarms, and simple controls.

## Key Features & Capabilities
-   **Burglar detection:** When a door opens, the system checks for nearby approved devices (e.g., a user's phone); unrecognized entries are flagged as unauthorized.
-   **Versatile keypad:** Users can arm/disarm without a phone.
-   **Lock reminder:** Sends a notification if the user leaves a defined safe zone without locking the door.
-   **Alarm system:** Triggers an on-device alarm upon intrusion and sends instant mobile alerts to approved users.
-   **Real-time tracking:** Shows last-seen time/place, enables a "ping" to locate the device, and includes a Lost Mode.
-   **Multi-user/device access:** Multiple approved users can control the device and receive notifications.
-   **Cellular connectivity (optional):** Maintains alerts during internet outages; paired with the built-in battery for continued operation.
-   **Mobile app control:** Monitor status, receive alerts, and adjust settings remotely.

## Target Users & Use Cases
Stated audiences include college students, renters, and travelers using dorms, apartments, sublets, and short-term stays. The device is positioned for everyday protection in shared or temporary spaces and for situations with unreliable networks.

## Development Status
According to the page, development began in late 2022. The team references "final prototypes," a brief demo, and a product evolution overview.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
The team states it is moving from final prototypes into scaled production and has prepared contingency plans for potential schedule shifts, supported by relationships with suppliers and manufacturing partners. No specific calendar dates are listed. As a proposed next step to validate a core use case, the team plans to conduct a post-campaign pilot test. This planned pilot test would involve a defined user group, such as 50 students in a dormitory setting, to gather evidence on the performance and usability of the multi-user access and notification features in a real-world shared environment. The specific, measurable outcomes we intend to capture include user activation rate, overall system reliability in a multi-user scenario, and notification accuracy, with a proposed target of >95% accuracy in distinguishing authorized from unauthorized entries. Furthermore, as a proposed preliminary step before this pilot, the team plans to conduct a small, focused test of the lock reminder feature's geofencing accuracy in a defined urban environment, with a proposed goal of 90% accuracy within a 100-meter radius. Additionally, the team proposes a small test to validate the built-in battery's performance during a simulated internet outage, specifying a proposed 48-hour continuous operation test. To specifically address the reliability of the core 'approved-device proximity check' feature, the team also proposes a small, focused test to validate its performance in a dense, multi-device environment (like a dorm hallway), with a proposed accuracy target of correctly identifying an authorized user's device 95% of the time within a 3-meter range. To specifically address the physical robustness required for a portable device used by travelers, the team also proposes a small, focused test to validate the device's physical durability, specifying a proposed test like 'a drop test from 1 meter onto a hard surface to verify continued functionality'.

## Risks & Challenges
Acknowledged risks include supply-chain delays during scale-up and the complexity of supporting multi-user, multi-device scenarios across varied environments. Mitigations include established partner relationships and a focus on keeping the experience simple but secure. The proposed pilot test plan is designed to specifically address the challenge of validating multi-user scenarios by measuring the outcomes noted above, including the proposed notification accuracy target. The proposed small test of the geofencing accuracy, with its proposed goal of 90% accuracy within a 100-meter radius, is intended to specifically address potential performance variability of the lock reminder feature in dense urban settings. The proposed small test of the built-in battery's performance is intended to specifically address the reliability of the device during extended power or internet outages. The proposed small test of the 'approved-device proximity check' in a dense environment is intended to specifically address potential signal interference and accuracy challenges in real-world, high-traffic settings. The proposed small test of physical durability is intended to specifically address the risk of device failure due to accidental drops during travel or frequent relocation.

## Team & Partnerships
The founders describe themselves as students and renters who built the product around their lived constraints. They reference suppliers and manufacturing partners without naming them. The team also discloses the use of an AI text-to-speech system for a campaign video voice-over.

## What's Included
A mobile app experience for remote control/alerts is described. The campaign also mentions an initial free trial period for the product's subscription service. Variants include a Wi-Fi model and an option with cellular connectivity.

## Technical Details
Explicit details include optional cellular connectivity, an on-device keypad, an on-device alarm, approved-device proximity checks, and a built-in battery supporting operation during internet outages. Specific dimensions, materials, and OS requirements are not listed.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team emphasizes ongoing commitment to a simple, secure experience as the product scales; ongoing software update cadence or warranty terms are not detailed. The proposed pilot test with a student group, including the measurement of activation rate and the proposed target for notification accuracy, would be part of the planned post-launch validation efforts. The proposed small test of geofencing accuracy in an urban environment, with its proposed goal of 90% accuracy within a 100-meter radius, is also a planned component of these validation efforts. The proposed small test of the built-in battery's performance is a planned component of these validation efforts. The proposed small test of the 'approved-device proximity check' in a dense environment, with its proposed accuracy target, is a planned component of these validation efforts. The proposed small test of physical durability is a planned component of these validation efforts.

## One-Sentence Summary
A compact, portable home-security device that installs without tools or Wi-Fi, offering app control, on-device alerts, and shared access for renters, students, and travelers.

## Problem
The creators argue that traditional residential security is expensive, invasive, and built for homeowners, leaving students, renters, and travelers without a practical way to feel secure in dorms, sublets, and temporary stays. They cite barriers such as landlord approval, drilling, and long-term contracts as key blockers.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is a lease-friendly smart security device designed to be set up in minutes without tools or approvals. It works without Wi-Fi (with an optional cellular version) and provides peace of mind across dorms, apartments, and travel accommodations through mobile alerts, local alarms, and simple controls.

## Key Features & Capabilities
-   **Burglar detection:** When a door opens, the system checks for nearby approved devices (e.g., a user's phone); unrecognized entries are flagged as unauthorized.
-   **Versatile keypad:** Users can arm/disarm without a phone.
-   **Lock reminder:** Sends a notification if the user leaves a defined safe zone without locking the door.
-   **Alarm system:** Triggers an on-device alarm upon intrusion and sends instant mobile alerts to approved users.
-   **Real-time tracking:** Shows last-seen time/place, enables a "ping" to locate the device, and includes a Lost Mode.
-   **Multi-user/device access:** Multiple approved users can control the device and receive notifications.
-   **Cellular connectivity (optional):** Maintains alerts during internet outages; paired with the built-in battery for continued operation.
-   **Mobile app control:** Monitor status, receive alerts, and adjust settings remotely.

## Target Users & Use Cases
Stated audiences include college students, renters, and travelers using dorms, apartments, sublets, and short-term stays. The device is positioned for everyday protection in shared or temporary spaces and for situations with unreliable networks.

## Development Status
According to the page, development began in late 2022. The team references "final prototypes," a brief demo, and a product evolution overview.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
The team states it is moving from final prototypes into scaled production and has prepared contingency plans for potential schedule shifts, supported by relationships with suppliers and manufacturing partners. No specific calendar dates are listed. As a proposed next step to validate a core use case, the team plans to conduct a post-campaign pilot test. This planned pilot test would involve a defined user group, such as 50 students in a dormitory setting, to gather evidence on the performance and usability of the multi-user access and notification features in a real-world shared environment. The specific, measurable outcomes we intend to capture include user activation rate, overall system reliability in a multi-user scenario, and notification accuracy, with a proposed target of >95% accuracy in distinguishing authorized from unauthorized entries. Furthermore, as a proposed preliminary step before this pilot, the team plans to conduct a small, focused test of the lock reminder feature's geofencing accuracy in a defined urban environment, with a proposed goal of 90% accuracy within a 100-meter radius. Additionally, the team proposes a small test to validate the built-in battery's performance during a simulated internet outage, specifying a proposed 48-hour continuous operation test. ## Problem
The creators argue that traditional residential security is expensive, invasive, and built for homeowners, leaving students, renters, and travelers without a practical way to feel secure in dorms, sublets, and temporary stays. They cite barriers such as landlord approval, drilling, and long-term contracts as key blockers.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is a lease-friendly smart security device designed to be set up in minutes without tools or approvals. It works without Wi-Fi (with an optional cellular version) and provides peace of mind across dorms, apartments, and travel accommodations through mobile alerts, local alarms, and simple controls.

## Key Features & Capabilities
-   **Burglar detection:** When a door opens, the system checks for nearby approved devices (e.g., a user's phone); unrecognized entries are flagged as unauthorized.
-   **Versatile keypad:** Users can arm/disarm without a phone.
-   **Lock reminder:** Sends a notification if the user leaves a defined safe zone without locking the door.
-   **Alarm system:** Triggers an on-device alarm upon intrusion and sends instant mobile alerts to approved users.
-   **Real-time tracking:** Shows last-seen time/place, enables a "ping" to locate the device, and includes a Lost Mode.
-   **Multi-user/device access:** Multiple approved users can control the device and receive notifications.
-   **Cellular connectivity (optional):** Maintains alerts during internet outages; paired with the built-in battery for continued operation.
-   **Mobile app control:** Monitor status, receive alerts, and adjust settings remotely.

## Target Users & Use Cases
Stated audiences include college students, renters, and travelers using dorms, apartments, sublets, and short-term stays. The device is positioned for everyday protection in shared or temporary spaces and for situations with unreliable networks.

This planned pilot test would involve a defined user group, such as 50 students in a dormitory setting, to gather evidence on the performance and usability of the multi-user access and notification features in a real-world shared environment. The specific, measurable outcomes we intend to capture include user activation rate, with a proposed target of >80% of pilot participants successfully activating and using the multi-user features within the first week; overall system reliability in a multi-user scenario; and notification accuracy, with a proposed target of >95% accuracy in distinguishing authorized from unauthorized entries. To specifically address the reliability of the core 'approved-device proximity check' feature, the team also proposes a small, focused test to validate its performance in a dense, multi-device environment (like a dorm hallway), with a proposed accuracy target of correctly identifying an authorized user's device 95% of the time within a 3-meter range. To specifically address the physical robustness required for a portable device used by travelers, the team also proposes a small, focused test to validate the device's physical durability, specifying a proposed test like 'a drop test from 1 meter onto a hard surface to verify continued functionality'.

## Risks & Challenges
Acknowledged risks include supply-chain delays during scale-up and the complexity of supporting multi-user, multi-device scenarios across varied environments. Mitigations include established partner relationships and a focus on keeping the experience simple but secure. The proposed pilot test plan is designed to specifically address the challenge of validating multi-user scenarios by measuring the outcomes noted above, including the proposed notification accuracy target and the proposed activation rate target of >80% within the first week. The proposed small test of the geofencing accuracy, with its proposed goal of 90% accuracy within a 100-meter radius, is intended to specifically address potential performance variability of the lock reminder feature in dense urban settings. The proposed small test of the 'approved-device proximity check' in a dense environment is intended to specifically address potential signal interference and accuracy challenges in real-world, high-traffic settings. The proposed small test of physical durability is intended to specifically address the risk of device failure due to accidental drops during travel or frequent relocation.

The founders describe themselves as students and renters who built the product around their lived constraints. They reference suppliers and manufacturing partners without naming them. The team also discloses the use of an AI text-to-speech system for a campaign video voice-over.

A mobile app experience for remote control/alerts is described. The campaign also mentions an initial free trial period for the product's subscription service. Variants include a Wi-Fi model and an option with cellular connectivity.

Explicit details include optional cellular connectivity, an on-device keypad, an on-device alarm, approved-device proximity checks, and a built-in battery supporting operation during internet outages. Specific dimensions, materials, and OS requirements are not listed.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team emphasizes ongoing commitment to a simple, secure experience as the product scales; ongoing software update cadence or warranty terms are not detailed. The proposed pilot test with a student group, including the measurement of activation rate with the proposed target of >80% within the first week and the proposed target for notification accuracy, would be part of the planned post-launch validation efforts. The proposed small test of geofencing accuracy in an urban environment, with its proposed goal of 90% accuracy within a 100-meter radius, is also a planned component of these validation efforts. The proposed small test of the built-in battery's performance is a planned component of these validation efforts. The proposed small test of the 'approved-device proximity check' in a dense environment, with its proposed accuracy target, is a planned component of these validation efforts. The proposed small test of physical durability is a planned component of these validation efforts.

## One-Sentence Summary
A compact, portable home-security device that installs without tools or Wi-Fi, offering app control, on-device alerts, and shared access for renters, students, and travelers.

## Problem
The creators argue that traditional residential security is expensive, invasive, and built for homeowners, leaving students, renters, and travelers without a practical way to feel secure in dorms, sublets, and temporary stays. They cite barriers such as landlord approval, drilling, and long-term contracts as key blockers.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is a lease-friendly smart security device designed to be set up in minutes without tools or approvals. It works without Wi-Fi (with an optional cellular version) and provides peace of mind across dorms, apartments, and travel accommodations through mobile alerts, local alarms, and simple controls.

## Key Features & Capabilities
-   **Burglar detection:** When a door opens, the system checks for nearby approved devices (e.g., a user's phone); unrecognized entries are flagged as unauthorized.
-   **Versatile keypad:** Users can arm/disarm without a phone.
-   **Lock reminder:** Sends a notification if the user leaves a defined safe zone without locking the door.
-   **Alarm system:** Triggers an on-device alarm upon intrusion and sends instant mobile alerts to approved users.
-   **Real-time tracking:** Shows last-seen time/place, enables a "ping" to locate the device, and includes a Lost Mode.
-   **Multi-user/device access:** Multiple approved users can control the device and receive notifications.
-   **Cellular connectivity (optional):** Maintains alerts during internet outages; paired with the built-in battery for continued operation.
-   **Mobile app control:** Monitor status, receive alerts, and adjust settings remotely.

## Target Users & Use Cases
Stated audiences include college students, renters, and travelers using dorms, apartments, sublets, and short-term stays. The device is positioned for everyday protection in shared or temporary spaces and for situations with unreliable networks.

## Development Status
According to the page, development began in late 2022. The team references "final prototypes," a brief demo, and a product evolution overview.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
The team states it is moving from final prototypes into scaled production and has prepared contingency plans for potential schedule shifts, supported by relationships with suppliers and manufacturing partners. No specific calendar dates are listed. As a proposed next step to validate a core use case, the team plans to conduct a post-campaign pilot test. This planned pilot test would involve a defined user group, such as 50 students in a dormitory setting, to gather evidence on the performance and usability of the multi-user access and notification features in a real-world shared environment. The specific, measurable outcomes we intend to capture include user activation rate, with a proposed target of >80% of pilot participants successfully activating and using the multi-user features within the first week; overall system reliability in a multi-user scenario; and notification accuracy, with a proposed target of >95% accuracy in distinguishing authorized from unauthorized entries. Furthermore, as a proposed preliminary step before this pilot, the team plans to conduct a small, focused test of the lock reminder feature's geofencing accuracy in a defined urban environment, with a proposed goal of 90% accuracy within a 100-meter radius. Additionally, the team proposes a small test to validate the built-in battery's performance during a simulated internet outage, specifying a proposed 48-hour continuous operation test. To specifically address the reliability of the core 'approved-device proximity check' feature, the team also proposes a small, focused test to validate its performance in a dense, multi-device environment (like a dorm hallway), with a proposed accuracy target of correctly identifying an authorized user's device 95% of the time within a 3-meter range. To specifically address the physical robustness required for a portable device used by travelers, the team also proposes a small, focused test to validate the device's physical durability, specifying a proposed test like 'a drop test from 1 meter onto a hard surface to verify continued functionality'. To specifically address the reliability of the optional cellular connectivity in challenging network conditions, the team also proposes a small, focused test to validate its performance in a low-signal environment, specifying a proposed goal like 'maintains alert transmission with >90% success rate in areas with 1 bar of signal'.

## Risks & Challenges
Acknowledged risks include supply-chain delays during scale-up and the complexity of supporting multi-user, multi-device scenarios across varied environments. Mitigations include established partner relationships and a focus on keeping the experience simple but secure. The proposed pilot test plan is designed to specifically address the challenge of validating multi-user scenarios by measuring the outcomes noted above, including the proposed notification accuracy target and the proposed activation rate target of >80% within the first week. The proposed small test of the geofencing accuracy, with its proposed goal of 90% accuracy within a 100-meter radius, is intended to specifically address potential performance variability of the lock reminder feature in dense urban settings. The proposed small test of the built-in battery's performance is intended to specifically address the reliability of the device during extended power or internet outages. The proposed small test of the 'approved-device proximity check' in a dense environment is intended to specifically address potential signal interference and accuracy challenges in real-world, high-traffic settings. The proposed small test of physical durability is intended to specifically address the risk of device failure due to accidental drops during travel or frequent relocation. The proposed small test of cellular connectivity in a low-signal environment is intended to specifically address the risk of alert failure for users in areas with poor cellular coverage.

## Team & Partnerships
The founders describe themselves as students and renters who built the product around their lived constraints. They reference suppliers and manufacturing partners without naming them. The team also discloses the use of an AI text-to-speech system for a campaign video voice-over.

## What's Included
A mobile app experience for remote control/alerts is described. The campaign also mentions an initial free trial period for the product's subscription service. Variants include a Wi-Fi model and an option with cellular connectivity.

## Technical Details
Explicit details include optional cellular connectivity, an on-device keypad, an on-device alarm, approved-device proximity checks, and a built-in battery supporting operation during internet outages. Specific dimensions, materials, and OS requirements are not listed.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team emphasizes ongoing commitment to a simple, secure experience as the product scales; ongoing software update cadence or warranty terms are not detailed. The proposed pilot test with a student group, including the measurement of activation rate with the proposed target of >80% within the first week and the proposed target for notification accuracy, would be part of the planned post-launch validation efforts. The proposed small test of geofencing accuracy in an urban environment, with its proposed goal of 90% accuracy within a 100-meter radius, is also a planned component of these validation efforts. The proposed small test of the built-in battery's performance is a planned component of these validation efforts. The proposed small test of the 'approved-device proximity check' in a dense environment, with its proposed accuracy target, is a planned component of these validation efforts. The proposed small test of physical durability is a planned component of these validation efforts.
